recipes.title: Gong bao chicken
recipes.description: Diced chicken with peanuts and dried chillies in a sauce where the vinegar matters more than the sugar.
steps: Mix the chicken with the egg white, a spoon of cornflour, a spoon of soy and a pinch of salt, and leave it twenty minutes.
Mix the sauce in advance: vinegar, the rest of the soy, the sugar and the rest of the cornflour with two spoons of water. Keep it within reach — there is no time to mix it later.
Heat the oil and fry the chillies with the Sichuan pepper for twenty seconds, until dark but not black. Burnt chilli turns bitter.
Add the chicken and leave it alone for a minute, then toss and cook through — two minutes more.
Throw in the garlic, ginger and the white of the spring onion, then after half a minute pour in the sauce. It thickens in seconds. Off the heat, add the peanuts and the green of the onion.

recipes.title: Jiaozi dumplings
recipes.description: Pork and cabbage dumplings, fried and then steamed in the same covered pan.
steps: Knead a dough from the flour and warm water for eight minutes and rest it under film for half an hour.
Salt the shredded cabbage and leave it fifteen minutes, then squeeze it dry by hand.
Work the pork with the ginger, soy and sesame oil in one direction, trickling in the stock until the mass turns tacky. Fold in the cabbage and spring onion.
Roll eight-centimetre rounds, thinner at the edge and thicker in the middle. Add filling and pleat one side shut.
Heat the oil in a pan, set the dumplings in seam up and fry three minutes to a golden base.
Pour in a hundred millilitres of water and cover at once. After seven minutes take the lid off and let the water go, back to a crisp base.

recipes.title: Miso soup
recipes.description: A soup of dashi and miso that takes ten minutes. Miso must never boil: boiling takes out both the aroma and the point of it.
steps: Cover the kombu with cold water and set it over low heat. Bring it to the edge of a boil over about ten minutes and lift the seaweed out before bubbles appear.
Bring the water to the boil, add the bonito flakes, take it off the heat at once and let it stand for two minutes until the flakes sink.
Strain the stock through a sieve without pressing the flakes — pressed flakes turn it bitter.
Soak the wakame in cold water for five minutes; it swells several times over.
Warm the dashi, add the tofu and the wakame and hold it at a low heat for a couple of minutes.
Whisk the miso smooth in a ladle of the hot stock, stir it back in and take the pan off the heat immediately. Scatter over the spring onion.

recipes.title: Katsudon
recipes.description: A breaded pork cutlet finished in sweet-salt broth with egg and slid onto rice.
steps: Nick the fat rim of each cutlet in a few places so they do not curl, season them and coat in flour, then egg, then panko.
Deep-fry at 170 °C for three minutes a side until golden. Drain on a rack rather than paper, so the underside stays crisp.
Cut the cutlets into strips a centimetre and a half wide without moving them apart — the shape matters when you serve.
In a small pan bring the dashi, soy, mirin and sugar to the boil, add the onion and cook for three minutes until soft.

Slide the cutlet into the broth, pour two thirds of the loosely beaten egg around it and cover for a minute. Add the rest, cover for twenty seconds more and take it off — the top layer of egg should stay loose.
Slide everything in the pan onto the rice in one movement, sauce and all.

recipes.title: Shoyu ramen
recipes.description: Broth, tare and oil — three separate things assembled in the bowl rather than cooked together.
steps: Cover the carcasses with cold water, boil for ten minutes and pour it away. Rinse the bones and the pot: the clarity of the broth depends on it.
Cover again with fresh water, add the ginger and garlic and simmer for three hours. Put the kombu in twenty minutes before the end and lift it out before it boils — boiled kombu turns bitter.
For the tare, reduce the soy, mirin, sake and shiitake to a third. What is left is a thick dark liquid — two spoons per bowl.
Boil the eggs for six and a half minutes, cool them in iced water, peel and steep them in the leftover tare for two hours.
Boil the noodles separately, strictly to the time on the packet, drain and put them straight into bowls with the tare in the bottom.
Pour the hot broth over, stir once so the tare disperses, and lay on the pork, the egg and the spring onion. Finish with the sesame oil.

recipes.title: Gyudon
recipes.description: Thinly sliced beef simmered with onion in dashi, soy and mirin, over rice.
steps: Bring the dashi with the soy, mirin, sake, sugar and grated ginger to the boil in a wide pan.
Add the onion and simmer for five minutes over medium heat, until it turns translucent.
Lay the beef over the surface slice by slice rather than in a heap, and cook two or three minutes. Skim any foam.
Take it off the moment the beef loses its pink. Left longer it toughens within a minute.
Divide the rice between bowls, spoon the beef and onion over with two or three spoons of the broth, and serve with the pickled ginger.

recipes.title: Tempura
recipes.description: Vegetables and prawns in an ice-cold lumpy batter. Whisking it smooth is exactly what must not happen.
steps: Score the prawns three times on the inner curve and straighten them slightly, so they do not curl into rings in the oil.
Combine the dashi, soy and mirin, bring them to the boil and take them off: this is tentsuyu. Serve it with grated daikon.
Heat the oil to 180 °C. Only when it is ready do you mix the batter — not before.
Beat the cold egg into the iced water, tip in the flour and cornflour and stir with chopsticks for five or six strokes. Leave the lumps.
Dust the pieces in dry flour, dip them in the batter and lower them in three or four at a time. Fry ninety seconds to two minutes.
Drain on a rack, never on paper. Between batches skim the floating scraps of batter out of the oil: they burn and taint the flavour.

recipes.title: Okonomiyaki
recipes.description: A thick cabbage pancake where the batter only binds. Yam in the batter gives it the airy texture.
steps: Mix the flour, grated yam and dashi and rest it half an hour in the fridge: the batter comes together better.
Fold the eggs into the batter, then the cabbage, spring onion and tenkasu. Fold from underneath and briefly: the cabbage must not start weeping.
Mound a quarter of the mixture onto a hot pan in a fifteen-centimetre round and do not flatten it: the air inside is wanted.
Lay slices of pork belly on top and cook five minutes covered over medium heat.
Turn it with two spatulas in one decisive movement and cook five minutes more, this time uncovered.
Brush with okonomi sauce, pipe lines of mayonnaise and drag a cocktail stick across them. Scatter over katsuobushi and aonori.

recipes.title: Nikujaga
recipes.description: Beef and potato simmered in dashi with soy and mirin. The classic of Japanese home cooking.
steps: Cut the potatoes into large pieces and soak them ten minutes in cold water to lose the surface starch.
Fry the onion in oil for two minutes, add the thinly sliced beef and cook until it loses its pink.
Add the potato and carrot and turn them so they take on the fat from the meat.
Add the dashi, sake and sugar, bring it up and skim.
Cover with an otoshibuta or a foil disc with a hole in it and simmer ten minutes over medium heat.
Add the soy and mirin and simmer fifteen minutes more, until only a little liquid is left at the bottom.
Add the beans for the last three minutes, take it off the heat and let it stand twenty minutes.

recipes.title: Bibimbap
recipes.description: Rice under separately cooked vegetables, meat and an egg, mixed with gochujang right before eating.
steps: Marinate the beef in soy, garlic and a spoon of sesame oil for twenty minutes.
Blanch the spinach for thirty seconds, squeeze it dry and dress with sesame oil and a pinch of salt. Boil the sprouts three minutes and dress them the same way, with garlic.
Fry the carrot and the mushrooms separately, a couple of minutes each, seasoning each on its own. No need to wash the pan in between.
Sear the beef over a high flame for two minutes. Fry the eggs separately, leaving the yolks runny.
Divide the hot rice between bowls, arrange the vegetables and beef in sections, and top with an egg and a spoon of gochujang. Each person does the mixing.

recipes.title: Galbijjim
recipes.description: Beef short ribs braised in soy with pear, until the meat falls from the bone.
steps: Soak the ribs in cold water for an hour, changing it twice, until the water runs clear.
Blanch the ribs in boiling water for five minutes, drain and rinse them under cold water.
Blend the pear, onion, garlic and ginger to a smooth purée.
Mix the purée with the soy, sugar, mirin and sesame oil and pour it over the ribs.
Bring it up, skim, and braise covered for an hour and a half on a low heat.
Add the carrot, daikon, mushrooms, chestnuts and jujubes and braise twenty-five minutes more.
Uncover and reduce the sauce to a gloss, spooning it over the ribs. Scatter with spring onion.

recipes.title: Samgyetang
recipes.description: A whole young chicken stuffed with glutinous rice and ginseng, simmered in its own broth.
steps: Soak the glutinous rice in cold water for two hours and drain it.
Rinse the birds, trim the excess fat at the cavity and pat them dry.
Fill each cavity two-thirds with rice, adding a ginseng root, garlic, a chestnut and a jujube.
Cross the legs and tuck one through a slit in the other; the cavity then closes without string.
Pack the birds into a pot and add cold water just to cover them.
Bring it up, skim, and simmer for an hour and a quarter.
Serve each bird in its own bowl of broth, with salt and pepper on a separate saucer.

recipes.title: Pad thai
recipes.description: Rice noodles fried with tamarind, fish sauce and palm sugar. The whole thing takes four minutes.
steps: Soak the noodles in warm water for twenty minutes. They should bend but still feel firm when you bite one.
Dissolve the palm sugar in the tamarind and fish sauce, warming them together for a minute. Taste it: sour, salty and sweet should all land equally.
Get the wok hot, fry the tofu until crisp, add the garlic and shallot, then after half a minute the prawns. Cook until pink and push them to the side.
Break the eggs into the cleared space, let them set and break them up with the spatula. Add the drained noodles and pour in the sauce.
Fry, tossing constantly, for two minutes until the noodles drink the sauce and soften. Add the sprouts and chives, toss once and take it off.

recipes.title: Pad krapow
recipes.description: Minced pork fried with chilli, garlic and holy basil. Five minutes from start to plate.
steps: Pound the garlic and chillies to a rough paste in a mortar. A mortar gives a different result from a knife: the juices come out and reach the oil.
Mix the oyster, fish and soy sauces with the sugar in a cup — there will be no time once the pan is hot.
Heat the wok with two spoons of oil, throw in the paste and fry for twenty seconds, to the smell.
Add the pork and leave it alone for a minute, then break it up and fry two minutes more. Pour in the sauce and let it coat the meat.
Off the heat, stir in the basil — the residual heat wilts it in seconds. In the same pan fry the eggs in the rest of the oil until the edges go lacy.

recipes.title: Khao soi
recipes.description: Northern Thai noodles in coconut curry, boiled noodles in the broth and fried ones on top.
steps: Set a fifth of the noodles aside, separate the strands and deep-fry them to a golden crisp.
Heat the thick part of the coconut milk in a pan, without stirring, until the oil separates out.
Fry the curry paste, curry powder and turmeric in that oil for three minutes, until deeply fragrant.
Add the chicken and turn it in the paste until it is coated all over.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and some water, the fish sauce and the sugar, and simmer thirty minutes.
Boil the remaining noodles and divide them between bowls.
Ladle over the curry and chicken, top with the fried noodles, shallot, pickled greens, coriander and a wedge of lime.

recipes.title: Massaman curry
recipes.description: A mild curry of beef, potato and peanuts, built on spices of the Muslim tradition.
steps: Heat the thick part of the coconut milk without stirring until the oil separates.
Fry the massaman paste in that oil for four minutes, until it darkens and smells right.
Add the beef and turn it in the paste, then add the cinnamon, cardamom and bay.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and stew gently for an hour, until the meat is tender.
Add the potato and onion in large pieces and cook twenty minutes more.
Stir in the tamarind, palm sugar and fish sauce and taste: it should read sweet, sour and salty at once.
Add the peanuts, warm them five minutes and serve with jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Phở bò
recipes.description: A clear beef broth with charred ginger and whole spices, rice noodles, and beef that finishes cooking in the bowl.
steps: Cover the bones with cold water, bring to the boil and let them go for ten minutes. Throw the water away, rinse the bones under the tap and wash the pot. This step is what buys you a clear broth.
Halve the onion and ginger and char the cut faces in a dry pan or straight over the flame until they blacken in patches.
Toast the spices in a dry pan until they smell, then tie them in muslin. Return the bones to the clean pot with the brisket, onion, ginger and spices, and cover with water three fingers above.
Simmer for three hours at the barest tremble. Skim for the first half hour. Lift the brisket out after ninety minutes and let it cool.
Strain the broth through a fine sieve and season with fish sauce and sugar. Taste it: it should be slightly saltier than pleasant to drink on its own, because the noodles will take their share.
Cook the noodles and divide them between bowls. Lay the sliced brisket and the raw sirloin on top. Ladle boiling broth over so it covers the meat, and serve the herbs, lime and chilli alongside.

recipes.title: Bánh mì
recipes.description: A French baguette with Vietnamese filling: pâté, pork, pickled vegetables and coriander in one sandwich.
steps: Stir the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt into 100 ml of warm water until dissolved. Pour it over the carrot and daikon and leave for an hour at room temperature.
Marinate the pork in fish sauce with a spoon of sugar for twenty minutes, then sear it over a high flame for three minutes a side, until the edges caramelise.
Warm the baguettes at 200 °C for five minutes so the crust crisps again. Split them lengthways, not all the way through.
Spread pâté on one half and mayonnaise on the other. Layer in the pork, the drained pickles, cucumber, coriander and chilli. Press it shut with your palm and serve at once.

recipes.title: Dal tadka
recipes.description: A lentil stew finished by pouring sizzling spiced fat over it. That step is the dish.

Add the cumin at once, the garlic and chillies ten seconds later, the asafoetida twenty seconds after that. The whole thing takes under a minute and cannot be left alone.
Pour the sizzling tadka straight into the lentils — it should hiss. Stir once and serve with rice or flatbread.

recipes.title: Chicken biryani
recipes.description: Rice and marinated chicken finished together under a lid: the layers cook in steam rather than by stirring.

recipes.title: Spaghetti carbonara
recipes.description: Pasta from four ingredients: guanciale, eggs, pecorino and pepper. There is no cream in it and never was.

recipes.title: Risotto alla milanese
recipes.description: A saffron risotto built on stock and near-constant stirring, which is what pulls the starch out of the rice and makes it creamy.
steps: Steep the saffron in a ladle of hot stock and set it aside. Keep the rest of the stock at a bare simmer — cold stock stops the cooking.
Melt half the butter and sweat the onion over low heat until soft and translucent without letting it colour, about eight minutes.
Add the rice and stir for a couple of minutes until the grains are translucent at the edges and milky in the centre. This is the tostatura, and it keeps the grains intact.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely — the smell of alcohol has to go.
Add the stock a ladle at a time, stirring, waiting until the rice has nearly absorbed it before the next. Around eighteen minutes, until the grain is soft outside with a slight bite in the middle.
Stir in the saffron infusion, take the pan off the heat and beat in the cold butter and parmesan, shaking the pan hard. The risotto should spread slowly across the plate.

recipes.title: Tiramisu
recipes.description: Savoiardi in coffee under a mascarpone cream. No baking, but two places where it can go wrong.

Mix the coffee with the marsala. Dip each savoiardo for one second a side and lay them in a tight layer in the dish.
Spread half the cream, level it, then repeat the biscuit and cream layers. Cover and refrigerate for at least six hours, better overnight.
Dust with cocoa through a sieve right before serving. Do it in advance and the cocoa takes on moisture and goes blotchy.

recipes.title: Pizza margherita
recipes.description: A long-fermented dough, uncooked tomato, mozzarella and basil. Time decides everything here, not the number of ingredients.
steps: Dissolve the yeast in the water, add the flour and mix to a rough dough. Rest it twenty minutes, then work in the salt and knead ten minutes to a smooth ball.

Take the dough out three hours before baking. Crush the tomatoes by hand with a pinch of salt: the sauce is done.

recipes.description: A Provençal vegetable stew where each vegetable is cooked separately before they meet — otherwise it turns to mush.
steps: Fry the aubergine over high heat in two spoons of oil until the edges brown, then set it aside. Aubergine drinks oil instantly — do not add more, it gives it back later.

Fry the pepper until soft with a few charred spots and set it aside as well.
In the remaining oil, sweat the onion until soft, add the garlic and thyme and give it half a minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and cook them down over medium heat into a thick sauce, about twenty minutes. It should hold on a spoon rather than run off it.
Return the vegetables to the pan, season and warm them through together for ten minutes over low heat. Take it off, add the basil and let it stand — ratatouille is better warm than hot.

recipes.title: French onion soup

recipes.title: Quiche lorraine
recipes.description: A shortcrust base with bacon and a cream and egg custard. No cheese and no onion — the classical recipe has neither.
steps: Cut the cold butter into the flour with a pinch of salt to a crumb, add the egg and iced water and bring the dough together without kneading. Chill it an hour.

recipes.title: Croissant
recipes.description: A laminated yeasted dough with twenty-seven layers of butter. Temperature decides everything: dough and butter must be equally cold.
steps: Mix the flour, cold milk, yeast, sugar, salt and softened butter for five minutes. No longer: strong gluten fights the rolling later.
Flatten the dough into a rectangle, wrap it and refrigerate at least four hours, better overnight.
Beat the cold butter with a rolling pin into a centimetre-thick square and keep it cold. It should bend without cracking or melting.
Roll the dough to twice the size of the butter square, lay the butter in the middle and fold the edges over it like an envelope, sealing the seams.
Roll it into a long rectangle and fold it in three. Chill forty minutes. Repeat twice more — three folds in all.
Roll the dough to four millimetres, cut triangles with a ten-centimetre base and roll each from the base to the tip, stretching gently.
Prove two hours at 25 °C — no warmer, or the butter runs out. Glaze with egg and bake at 200 °C for eighteen minutes.

recipes.title: Paella valenciana
recipes.description: Rice in a wide pan with chicken, rabbit and beans. It is never stirred once, and the crust on the bottom depends on that.

Pour in the stock, add the rosemary, saffron and white beans, salt it noticeably harder than feels right and let it boil for ten minutes. This is the last moment you can correct the seasoning.
Scatter the rice in an even layer and level it once with a spoon. After that do not touch the pan again — no stirring, no smoothing.
Cook on a high flame for ten minutes, then drop to medium for another eight, until the stock is gone. The rice should be showing above the surface.
Turn the heat up for half a minute and listen: the moment the sound turns from bubbling to a dry crackle, take it off. That is the socarrat. Cover with a cloth and let it stand for five minutes.

recipes.title: Ham croquetas
recipes.description: A thick béchamel with ham, chilled until firm, breadcrumbed and deep-fried.

recipes.title: Sticky toffee pudding
recipes.description: A moist date sponge under a hot sauce of cream and dark sugar.
steps: Cover the chopped dates with a cup of boiling water and the bicarbonate and leave them fifteen minutes.
Mash the dates with a fork into a coarse paste, water and all.
Beat a hundred grams of the butter with a hundred and fifty of the sugar until pale, adding the eggs one by one.
Fold in the flour with the baking powder, then the date paste; the batter comes out loose, which is correct.
Pour it into a greased tin and bake at 180 °C for thirty-five minutes, to a skewer that comes out with moist crumbs.
Melt the remaining butter with the remaining sugar and the cream and cook the sauce five minutes to thicken.
Prick the warm sponge with a skewer, pour over half the sauce and serve the rest in a jug.

recipes.title: Käsespätzle
recipes.description: Swabian egg noodles layered with cheese and buried under fried onion.
steps: Mix the flour, eggs, water, salt and nutmeg and beat the dough with a spoon for a good five minutes, until bubbles rise and it starts to string off the spoon.
While the dough rests, fry the onion in butter over medium heat until deep gold. That is twenty minutes, not five — the sugars need the time to caramelise.
Press the dough into boiling salted water through a spätzle grater or a wide-holed colander. They float within a minute; lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Layer them into a warm dish: spätzle, cheese, spätzle, cheese. The heat of the noodles melts it; no oven is needed.
Bury it under the fried onion and serve at once. The classic side is a green salad with a vinegar dressing, and it is a counterweight rather than a garnish.

recipes.title: Sauerbraten
recipes.description: Beef steeped for days in a vinegar marinade and braised in it, with a gravy thickened on gingerbread.
steps: Boil the vinegar with the wine, vegetables and spices, cool it completely and pour it over the beef. Keep it in the fridge three to five days, turning once a day.
Lift the meat out, dry it with kitchen paper and brown it hard on every side in a hot casserole. Strain the marinade, keeping the vegetables.
Fry the marinated vegetables in the same fat, add the sugar and let it catch a little colour. Pour in the marinade and bring it to the boil.
Return the meat, cover and braise over a low flame for two hours, turning it once halfway. A fork should meet no resistance.
Take the meat out and keep it warm. Stir the crumbled gingerbread and the raisins into the gravy and cook for fifteen minutes: the gingerbread dissolves and thickens it on its own.
Blend the gravy smooth and taste it for the balance of sour and sweet. Carve the meat across the grain and pour the gravy over.

recipes.title: Swabian potato salad
recipes.description: Potato dressed in warm stock with vinegar and oil. No mayonnaise — southern Germany does not admit it here.
steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins until done, about twenty minutes from the boil. Test with a knife: it should go in without dropping through.
While they cook, warm the stock with the onion, vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper, without letting it boil.
Peel the potatoes while hot, holding them on a fork, and slice them three or four millimetres thick straight into the bowl.
Pour the hot dressing over and leave it twenty minutes, turning it once. The potato drinks almost all of the liquid.
Add the oil, turn it again and taste. It should be slightly sharper than feels right; the flavour settles as it stands.

recipes.title: Schweinshaxe
recipes.description: Pork knuckle roasted to a glassy crackling, with dark beer and sauerkraut.
steps: Score the skin in diamonds every centimetre and a half, down to the fat but not into the meat.
Rub the knuckles with coarse salt, pepper, caraway and garlic, working it into the cuts.
Put them in a pot with the onion, carrot, celeriac and bay, and cover with beer and water.
Simmer for an hour, never letting it boil hard.
Move the knuckles to a tray, pat the skin dry and roast at 180 °C for an hour and twenty.
Every twenty minutes baste with beer from the pot and fat from the tray.
Raise the oven to 240 °C for the last ten minutes, until the crackling blisters.

recipes.title: Black Forest gateau
recipes.description: Chocolate sponge soaked in kirsch, with whipped cream and sour cherries.
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar over a water bath until warm, then beat them ten minutes to a thick pale foam.
Sift the flour with the cocoa and fold it in with a spatula in three additions, then the melted butter.
Bake the sponge at 175 °C for thirty-five minutes and cool it completely, ideally overnight.
Cut the sponge into three layers and soak each with cherry syrup mixed with kirsch.
Dissolve the gelatine, whip the cream with the icing sugar and add the gelatine in a thin stream.
Assemble: sponge, cream, cherries, cream again — three times over, finishing with cream.
Cover the sides and top with chocolate shavings, decorate with cherries and chill four hours.

recipes.title: Bacalhau à brás
recipes.description: Salt cod with matchstick potatoes and egg that binds everything without becoming an omelette.
steps: Poach the soaked cod for five minutes, cool it and pull it into flakes by hand, discarding skin and bones. By hand rather than with a fork: that is how small bones are found.
Deep-fry the potato matchsticks at 180 °C to a crisp gold, in batches. Drain on a rack and salt them.
In a wide pan sweat the onion in the olive oil for ten minutes until soft and sweet, adding the garlic for the last minute.
Add the cod and warm it through for three minutes, then tip in the potato and toss.
Take the pan off the heat, pour in the beaten eggs and stir without stopping for half a minute, until they turn creamy. Scatter over the parsley and olives.

recipes.title: Pastel de nata
recipes.description: Flaky pastry cases of custard baked in extreme heat until the surface blisters black.
steps: Boil the sugar and water to 100 °C and take it off. Separately bring the milk, cream, cinnamon and lemon peel to just below boiling.
Whisk the flour into a little cold milk until smooth and stir it into the hot mixture. Cook, stirring, to the thickness of soured cream.
Pour the hot syrup into the milk base in a thin stream, take it off the heat and stir in the yolks. Strain it and cool completely.
Roll the pastry into a tight log, cut two-centimetre discs and press each into a tin with your thumbs, taking the walls above the rim.
Heat the oven as high as it goes, at least 250 °C. Fill the cases three-quarters full and bake twelve to fifteen minutes, until the tops blister black.

recipes.title: Sardinhas assadas
recipes.description: Whole sardines salted coarsely and grilled over coals, served on a slice of bread.
steps: Rinse the sardines without gutting them and pat them dry on the outside.
Bury the fish in coarse salt on all sides and leave it half an hour at room temperature.
Light the coals and let them ash over; an open flame burns the skin within a minute.
Char the peppers on the coals, peel them and dress them with oil, garlic and vinegar.
Shake the excess salt off the fish and lay them on a hot, oiled grate.
Grill four minutes a side, turning them exactly once.
Lay the sardines on slices of bread and serve with boiled potatoes and the pepper salad.
